# Drafter notes — odyssey-076 (15.454–557)

Telemachus Comes Ashore: 63 units.

## Quotation handling
- Eumaeus’s speech from 15.390 runs on from odyssey-075 (its last unit closes only the inner ’ of the Phoenician woman’s speech). Unit 1 (454–456) therefore has no opening “ and no `mark`; the closing ” is on unit 19 (line 484, οὕτω τήνδε τε γαῖαν…). No inner quotation in this part, so no ‘ ’.
- Other speeches: Odysseus 486–492; Telemachus 503–507, 513–524, 536–538, 540–543; Theoclymenus 509–511, 531–534; Peiraeus 545–546. `mark` is on the first unit of each; “ and ” are in both `l` and `i`.
- 539 (ἦ καὶ Πείραιον προσεφώνεε) is a narrator’s line between two Telemachus speeches, so it is its own unit, not a continuation.

## Open points for the reviewer
1. **ἤχθετο (457).** Rendered "was loaded" (from ἄχθος), the traditional sense; the verb elsewhere means "be vexed". The note says so; the sense is not certain.
2. **ἠλέκτροισιν (460).** "amber"; the word also names the alloy electrum. Note says amber is the usual sense for beads.
3. **θῶκον … δήμοιό τε φῆμιν (468).** Taken as two parallel goals ("the seat of council and the talk of the people"); the sense of φῆμιν is flagged as uncertain.
4. **ἀεσιφροσύνῃσι (470).** "witlessness"; first element of unknown origin, stated in the note. The Greek is a plural abstract; the English is singular.
5. **κήξ (479).** Species unknown; `l` keeps "kex", `i` says "sea-bird".
6. **Artemis’s arrow (478).** Unbowdlerized: the woman is struck and thrown overboard (480–481).
7. **τελευτήσει κακὸν ἦμαρ (524).** Subject/object ambiguity (ἦμαρ neuter); English reads "an evil day will come to pass"; the note states the alternative.
8. **ὁδοιπόριον (506).** "provisions for the road", explained by the appositional δαῖτ’ ἀγαθήν; the exact sense of ὁδοιπόριον (provisions vs a gift) not certain.
9. **ἦ ἰθὺς … ἴω (511).** ἦ read as the interrogative particle, not ἤ "or"; English has no "Or".
10. **ἄλλως … καὶ ἡμέτερόνδε (513–514).** "even to our house" for καί; "also" is possible.
11. **εἰ γάρ κεν … μίμνοι (545).** Rendered "even if"; Greek is "for if … should stay". Noted.
12. **ἐπὶ χέρσου (495).** Left vague ("on the dry land" / "at the shore"); whether the ship has grounded is not said.
13. **ἱστός (496 mast, 517 loom).** One word, two senses, said in the notes; `l` "a loom she weaves" is literal but odd.
14. **κληΐς (549).** "rowing-benches"; the timber is unsettled and the note says so.
15. **οἱ in ἔνθα οἱ ἦσαν ὕες (556).** Read as looking ahead to the swineherd of the relative clause; English "he had swine".
16. **ταχύς "swift".** The table’s ταχύς row already gives "swift"; "swift" now serves θοός, ὠκύς and ταχύς.
17. **κοιρανέουσιν (510).** Taken from the table’s "play the lord" / "lord it", which carries a note of swagger; the Greek here is neutral. Kept for consistency; the note says the verb only means "hold power".
18. **ἐνδυκέως "kindly" beside ἤπιος "kind/gentle" and φιλέειν "treat as a friend".** Three kindly words in 488–491 and 542–543 kept apart as far as English allows.
19. **First σ in Ὀδυσεύς (485)** vs Ὀδυσσῆος (522, 554): noted in the unit for 485 as a metrical spelling.
20. **Part title.** "Telemachus Comes Ashore" (Τηλεμάχου ἄφιξις) names the larger action; the first third is the end of Eumaeus’s story.

## Repeated lines (English taken from the packet)
- 15.471: new unit (ends with ·, not the published full stop), English from the published line with the semicolon.
- 15.476, 477, 493, 501, 502, 525, 548, 554: first-clause/line wording from the packet; the units differ in extent, so none is a whole-unit repeat.
- 15.508, 512, 535: whole-unit repeats, `l` and `i` identical to the published ones.
